newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia seen getting IMF tranche despite delay.
newsitem.headline: Russia seen getting IMF tranche despite delay.

text.p: Russia looks set to get the latest tranche of its $10 billion International Monetary Fund loan, although payment may be held up for technical reasons, banking sources said on Tuesday.
They said the delay, which could mean the money will not be paid until after next week's IMF/World Bank annual meeting, should not be compared with the delay in July.
Concern over budget revenue and tax collection held up disbursement of that month's $330 million tranche, the seventh. Close to $2 billion of the loan has been disbursed.
Economists say Russia has met the IMF's monetary performance targets for August, but the Fund has some worries over the future level of foreign reserves.

Central Bank chairman Sergei Dubinin said earlier this month the bank had spent $1.6 billion in August to defend the rouble when a faster than usual decline in the currency had made short-term T-bill yields unattractive.
However, he said the bank had sufficient reserves to keep the rouble within its crawling-peg exchange rate corridor against the dollar.
Net reserves are one of the IMF's performance criteria. Gross central bank reserves in mid-July stood at $14.9 billion, Dubinin said in late July.

The central bank has set a series of daily exchange rate corridors for the second half of the year, designed to allow the rouble to depreciate gently and put it in a range of 5,500-6,100 to the dollar on December 31. It was bid at 5,400 late on Tuesday.
The rouble was at 5,352 to the dollar on the Moscow Interbank Curreny Exchange on September 2 and 5,211 on August 1.
